The three identified recoveries were approximately 150 seconds each, within the prescribed 120-180 second range.

coach_briefing: SpeedCoach supports completion of 4 x 500 m with continuous ~21 SPM work bouts and three ~150 s active recoveries at ~16 SPM, matching the distance, rate, and recovery-duration prescription. Use SpeedCoach for rate and interval distance; disregard mobile SPM. B2/B3 compliance and crew technique remain unverified.

plan_summary.summary: Planned water session: 4 x 500 m work intervals at 20-22 SPM, B2/B3, with 120-180 seconds of active light-rowing recovery; each work interval was to remain continuous.

session_associations.reason: The routes overlap closely, while the mobile record has a documented 18-second later clock start. The records also have nearly equal durations and closely similar total distances, despite a documented mobile distance bias.

source_policy.reason: SpeedCoach is selected because it supplies the interval distance structure. Mobile cumulative distance is documented as 0.476% higher and flagged for distance bias.
SpeedCoach contains positive SPM observations across the session. Mobile has zero positive-SPM rows and is explicitly flagged SPM_ALL_ZERO.
SpeedCoach supplies the interval-pattern timing windows. Mobile begins 18 seconds later, so its clock is not used as the timing baseline.
Both sources support route association, but SpeedCoach is retained as the primary session record because its telemetry also provides valid SPM and the interval structure.
